title: dedicated fleet autoscaler: burst controls + utilization reporting enhancements
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: Improve Dedicated fleet autoscaler's burst capacity controls and add higher-fidelity utilization reporting to help SREs and platform teams diagnose over/under-provisioning and to enforce throughput guarantees. This PR implements: 1) a token-based burst budget that decays over time per-fleet, 2) configurable per-customer burst windows and soft/hard caps, 3) exponential backoff-based throttling with graceful degradation paths (route to backup fleets or lower-cost model variants), 4) detailed utilization telemetry (per-device GPU utilization, queued request age histograms, burst budget consumption) exposed to Redwood Console and Prometheus, and 5) migration + upgrade safe defaults and rollout flags. Changes include runtime scheduler hooks, autoscaler policy additions, a new DB schema migration for burst_budget state, a set of integration tests simulating burst traffic, and Console dashboard widgets. Checklist: - [x] design doc: ENG-3492 linked - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs + console widgets - [x] canary rollout plan - [x] rollout tested on staging. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3492 and support ticket SUP-1123. Rollout: feature flag enabled by default for new Dedicated clusters; canaryed on two customers for 72h prior to full rollout.

review_comments: Diego Martinez (2026-02-16): Can you clarify the decay window and how it interacts with reserved capacity? Concern: aggressive decay might starve legitimate bursts in multi-tenant fleets.

Avery Chen (2026-02-16): Decay is per-fleet token bucket with half-life configurable via policy; default half-life is 15m. Reserved capacity is excluded from burst budget checks (burst only applies to surplus capacity), adding a unit test to assert this behavior.
Priya Singh (2026-02-18): Need a migration rollback path; if migration fails during rolling upgrade we should default to zeroed burst budgets rather than failing allocations.
Avery Chen (2026-02-18): Added migration to write zeroed rows for new clusters and made allocator tolerate missing rows by treating as zeroed. Added migration rollback SQL and tests.
Ethan Ross (2026-02-20): Integration tests flaked on first CI run because of timing; recommend increasing test determinism or mocking time for decay step.
Avery Chen (2026-02-20): Reworked integration to mock clock and reduced reliance on wall-clock sleeps. CI rerun green. Marking as ready for final review.
Priya Singh (2026-02-22): Approved — left minor nits (console i18n keys).
Diego Martinez (2026-02-23): Approved and sanity-checked metrics cardinality; added suggestion to aggregate per-cluster to avoid high-cardinality labels.
release_notes: Enhancements to Dedicated fleet autoscaler: configurable burst controls (per-customer windows and caps), burst token bucket with decay, exponential backoff throttling with graceful fallbacks, and improved utilization telemetry exposed in Console and Prometheus. No breaking changes; rollout behind feature flag with staged canary.
notes: Canary plan: enabled for two customers for 72h; monitor burst_budget_consumed and queue_age histograms
Follow-ups: add per-model variant burst profiles (ENG-3610)
Support ticket SUP-1123 tracked a customer complaint about short lived bursts causing throttling — this PR addresses that with soft caps and backoff routes
